# Book Portability in a Transition

by
Grier L. Rubeling, Founder/CEO - Advisor Transition Services/Staff My RIA

December 18, 2023

   

The success of transitioning a book of business hinges on various factors, with portability being a central concern. Portability refers to the ability of an advisor to transfer their relationships, assets, and revenue streams from one firm to another. In this article, I delve into 5 key considerations that help advisors understand the portability of their book and the options available to assist with the process.

**1 – Contractual Agreements**  
The first thing I tell any advisor considering a transition is to consult an attorney. Employment contracts should be reviewed thoroughly to determine if there are any restrictive covenants, the extent of any non-compete or non-solicit clauses, and what the confidentiality obligations are.
Information learned from this process will determine the applicability of the broker protocol, client information allowances, and other important information that could significantly impact a book’s portability.

**2 – Client Retention**  
A transition is the perfect time to deep dive into a book and determine exactly what you want your new business to look like, especially from a client profile standpoint. It’s important to govern whether individual existing clients are a fit for your proposed new model.

Consider the strength and depth of your current relationship, the willingness to subscribe to your investment philosophy, the level of trust afforded to you as a fiduciary, and the rapport you’ve built over time. You could have relationships that have shifted in focus, profitability, or fit over the years. A shift in your own situation is the perfect time to part ways with clients, by explaining why your new business model doesn’t meet their current needs.
In many cases, clients will automatically be reassigned to new advisors, and you can avoid the conversation altogether.

On the other hand, you may have clients that resist change and choose not to join you even when you want them to – a situation you can’t necessarily control. Consider the strength of the relationship, level of rapport, and where the clients’ loyalties lie (with you or the existing firm). The things you’re considering about your clients are the same things they’re considering about you. Control what you can control, but manage your expectations properly.

**3 – Securities Transferability**  
One of the biggest challenges going from a captive model to an independent model is the transferability of securities. Fee-only advisory practices are currently trending. While attractive, not all books of business can be seamlessly converted to an advisory model. A broker-dealer relationship might be required, and it’s important to know what assets belong where.
Some categories I like to consider are:

• Transferability of existing advisory assets

• Share class conversion requirements

• Detached asset requirements

• Held-direct business

• Brokerage assets

• Advisor-controlled assets

The transferability of existing advisory assets refers to the ability to move securities from one account to another (in-kind) using a simple transfer document. The custodian will review a list of your securities and present a report that shows the eligibility of each item, so you know where to make concessions.

Share class conversion requirements refer to the ability to convert the share class of a security once it transfers into an account. Many funds have a share class that can be held in an advisory account even if that wasn’t the share class purchased. It’s important to understand the timing and nuances of these situations.

Detached asset requirements refer to securities that don’t transfer in-kind, like some alternative investments.
They might be eligible to hold but need additional paperwork to make the switch. This also references proprietary products that are not eligible to be held at the new firm. Sometimes, those securities can be liquidated, but it’s not guaranteed. Held-direct business can be variable annuities, 529 plans, or mutual funds held away. Identifying the accounts holding these assets is imperative to success, as is the determination of what to do with them. Will you convert them to an advisory product, affiliate with a broker-dealer, or seek out an outsourced brokerage firm?

If you want the ability to hold brokerage assets and/or earn commissions, you need a broker-dealer. Advisor-controlled assets are things like fixed annuities and LTC. Items you need to deal with but that don’t require an advisory or brokerage account.
With regards to securities transferability, there’s no easy way to determine the complexity of the situation – it requires research, developing a clear understanding of your current situation, and crafting a plan for execution.

**4 – Account Types and Features**  
Another important subject to consider is account types and features. Many large broker-dealers offer services like banking, loans, and mortgages. Clients rely on the fact that all their assets are in one place. Consolidation of statements and integration of technology are major selling points. They push internal initiatives, and reward you for adopting certain features on your clients’ accounts. You need to understand what features will not be available to you through your new custodian, and you’ll need to communicate these facts to your clients and manage their expectations properly.

**5 – Operational Efficiencies**  
Not all firms are created equal.
Some focus on building out integrations and cutting costs on internal improvements. Others spend big bucks developing proprietary technology to assist with operations. Some spend a lot of time and money training their support staff in specific departments, and pride themselves on a high level of expertise. Others cross-train across multiple departments and focus on more general knowledge.

Either way, the technology and support at your new firm are likely going to differ significantly from what you have now. Evaluate the operational aspects of the transition, including the ease of transferring client accounts and assets. Assess the compatibility of the new firm’s technology and systems with your existing client data and portfolio management tools. Collaborate with your new firm’s transition team, or a third-party consultant, to ensure a seamless transfer of accounts, minimizing disruptions for clients.
Manage your and your team’s expectations so you can properly manage the expectations of your clients.

It’s all in the preparation. Develop a comprehensive transition plan that includes client communication strategies, legal, compliance, and operational procedures. Identify potential challenges and roadblocks and devise contingency plans to address them. Leverage the support of transition experts, consultants, and recruiters to streamline the process. Prioritize the needs and concerns of your clients throughout the transition. Make them active participants in the process by seeking their input and preferences. Personalize the transition experience to ensure clients feel valued and cared for during the move. Address any concerns and questions honestly, demonstrating your commitment to their financial well-being.

Determining the portability of your book of business is a critical step in the transition process.
A thorough understanding of contractual obligations, client relationships, communication, current holdings, and operational factors is essential. With careful planning, transparent communication, and the right support, advisors can successfully navigate the transition, while preserving and growing their client base.

## The Importance of Transitioning to Adulthood

Transitioning to adulthood is a significant milestone that every young person must undergo. It is a time of change, growth, and development, marked by excitement and challenges. For many young adults, transitioning to adulthood can be overwhelming, especially when uncertain about what lies ahead.

Independence and responsibility are at the core of transitioning to adulthood. Young adults must learn to take charge of their lives, make independent decisions, and navigate life’s challenges effectively.
This entails developing a sense of identity, establishing healthy relationships, building a career, and managing finances. However, the road to independence is not always smooth, and many young people face difficulties along the way.

That is why the role of launch therapy in aiding young adults during this transitional period is crucial. By providing guidance and support, launch therapy can assist young adults in developing the skills and confidence they need to overcome challenges and build a successful future.

## Challenges Faced by Young Adults

Transitioning into adulthood can present a myriad of challenges for young adults, especially those without adequate support. Here are some of the common obstacles:

|Challenges |Description |
| --- | --- |
|Managing Finances |Young adults may struggle with budgeting, paying bills, and making financial decisions. |
|Establishing a Career |Finding a fulfilling job that aligns with one’s interests and skills can be daunting, especially in a competitive job market. |
|Building Healthy Relationships |Developing and maintaining healthy relationships with romantic partners, friends, and family members can be challenging for young adults. Many young adults learn that behaviors that may have worked in their family have a negative effect on those outside. |
|Developing a Sense of Identity |Young adults may struggle with defining their sense of self, understanding their values, and navigating their place in the world. |
|Mental Health |Issues such as anxiety, depression , autism, borderline personality disorder, and ADHD can emerge or worsen during this transitional period. |

It’s important to note that these challenges are not mutually exclusive, and some young adults may encounter multiple obstacles simultaneously, which can be overwhelming.

    + _Addressing mental health concerns_ : Many young adults experience mental health challenges such as anxiety or depression during the transition to adulthood. Launch therapy can help individuals manage these concerns and develop coping strategies.

    + _Building confidence and self-esteem_ : Launch therapy can assist young adults in establishing a sense of identity and purpose.

**Parenting styles can affect their (adult) children’s independence**  
In some cases, parents’ approach to raising their children can significantly influence their child’s readiness for adulthood. For example, overprotective or “helicopter” parenting can hinder the development of critical life skills, including problem-solving and resilience, which are crucial to launching successfully into adulthood. Many well-intentioned parents can unwittingly “stunt” their children’s confidence to launch into adult independence while trying to “help” them not have to struggle.

> Do you see yourself or your family in one or more of these factors?
There are many practical ways you can help your child move beyond their difficulties and launch into adulthood, starting today!
> 
>

## Strategies to support your adult child’s launch into adulthood

Adopting one or more of these strategies can help your child assume adult responsibilities.

* **Encourage your child’s independence!** If your child has always relied on you to do things for him/her, think about which life skills your child can take on and how you can encourage your child to become more independent. Gradually but consistently introduce more responsibilities and opportunities for independence, with gradually increased expectations.   Some examples include contributing more to household chores, finding part-time work, or enrolling in a vocational course that can lead to employment.   Allow your young adult to make decisions, even if they lead to mistakes. Learning from errors is a crucial part of becoming a responsible adult.
* **Maintain open communication:** Before making bold changes or demands on your child, have an adult conversation about your concerns and your desire to help them succeed. Maintain an open and non-judgmental line of communication. Listen actively to their concerns and fears, offering support while encouraging them to be the ones to make their own decisions and take all the practical steps necessary to move forward.
* Have realistic expectations: Understand and acknowledge the challenges young adults face today. It’s a harsh world out there! Especially if your child is accustomed to depending on you, set realistic expectations and celebrate small achievements towards independence.
* **Get professional help:** A mental health professional with experience supporting young adults to move to adult life successfully can provide your young adult with tools to manage anxiety, improve self-esteem, and build problem-solving skills.

One resource that has proven to be effective in supporting young adults during this critical phase is launch therapy. Launch therapy is a specialized form of counseling that focuses on preparing young adults for the challenges of adulthood. Through a combination of individualized treatment plans, coaching sessions, and evidence-based techniques, launch therapy can help individuals overcome obstacles, develop important life skills, and achieve their goals.

### ey Takeaways:

1. Transitioning to adulthood can be challenging for many young adults.
2. L aunch therapy is a specialized form of counseling that supports young adults during this transitional period.
3. With the right guidance and support, the journey to adulthood can be empowering and transformative.

## Understanding Launch Therapy

Launch therapy is a type of therapy that focuses on helping young adults transition into adulthood.

...

### What Methods are Used in Launch Therapy?

Launch therapy uses various methods to support young adults in their transition to adulthood. Some of these methods may include:

    + Coaching
    + Counseling
    + Cognitive behavioral therapy
    + Mentoring
    + Group therapy
    + Life skills training
    + Immersion experience

The specific methods used in launch therapy will depend on the individual’s needs and goals.

## The Importance of Transitioning to Adulthood

Transitioning to adulthood is a significant milestone that every young person must undergo. It is a time of change, growth, and development, marked by excitement and challenges. For many young adults, transitioning to adulthood can be overwhelming, especially when uncertain about what lies ahead.

Independence and responsibility are at the core of transitioning to adulthood. Young adults must learn to take charge of their lives, make independent decisions, and navigate life’s challenges effectively.
This entails developing a sense of identity, establishing healthy relationships, building a career, and managing finances. However, the road to independence is not always smooth, and many young people face difficulties along the way.

That is why the role of launch therapy in aiding young adults during this transitional period is crucial. By providing guidance and support, launch therapy can assist young adults in developing the skills and confidence they need to overcome challenges and build a successful future.

## Challenges Faced by Young Adults

Transitioning into adulthood can present a myriad of challenges for young adults, especially those without adequate support. Here are some of the common obstacles:

|Challenges |Description |
| --- | --- |
|Managing Finances |Young adults may struggle with budgeting, paying bills, and making financial decisions. |
|Establishing a Career |Finding a fulfilling job that aligns with one’s interests and skills can be daunting, especially in a competitive job market. |
|Building Healthy Relationships |Developing and maintaining healthy relationships with romantic partners, friends, and family members can be challenging for young adults. Many young adults learn that behaviors that may have worked in their family have a negative effect on those outside. |
|Developing a Sense of Identity |Young adults may struggle with defining their sense of self, understanding their values, and navigating their place in the world. |
|Mental Health |Issues such as anxiety, depression , autism, borderline personality disorder, and ADHD can emerge or worsen during this transitional period. |

It’s important to note that these challenges are not mutually exclusive, and some young adults may encounter multiple obstacles simultaneously, which can be overwhelming.

## How Launch Therapy Helps
Launch therapy is a highly effective method for supporting young adults during their transition to independence. With a range of techniques and strategies, therapists can help individuals overcome common obstacles and achieve their goals. Here are some ways that launch therapy can help:

    + _Developing life skills_ : Launch therapy can provide guidance on practical skills such as budgeting, time management, and household chores. These skills are essential for independent living and can sometimes be overlooked in traditional therapy sessions.

    + _Addressing mental health concerns_ : Many young adults experience mental health challenges such as anxiety or depression during the transition to adulthood. Launch therapy can help individuals manage these concerns and develop coping strategies.

    + _Building confidence and self-esteem_ : Launch therapy can assist young adults in establishing a sense of identity and purpose.
